newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS - Mixed data help Australia bonds, US data looms.
newsitem.headline: RTRS - Mixed data help Australia bonds, US data looms.

text.p: *Australian bonds ended firm after a jump in the August unemployment rate stirred thoughts of another rate easing.
*Comments by RBA's Fraser helped the trend, but a looming spate of key U.S. data kept the lid on the long-end.

"Overall, today's labour force figures add to the case for the Reserve Bank to leave interest rates on hold. They show a steady, but gentle recovery in employment, and do not signal the need for a further "insurance" interest rate cut," said Andrew Pease, senior economist at Nomura Research Australia.
However, State Bank chief economist Hans Kunnen believes the unemployment rise should make the RBA think about a further cut.
"Such a move may restore confidence, the factor that seems to be missing as far as consumers are concerned. The jobs data increases the possibility of a rate cut in the December quarter", he added.

Meanwhile, Fraser, who retires later this month, told a parliamentary banking committee that the central bank would cut official rates again if the economy needed support and if there was a comfortable inflation outlook.
He also said that there was scope for the yield differential between Australia and U.S. to narrow further as inflation was expected to keep falling for a least another year.
S&P's upgrading of the state of Victoria to AA-plus had no impact on Treasury Corp of Victoria bonds, traders said.
"It (the upgrade) had been well priced in. In fact TCV trades already trades like a AAA," one trader said.

The Australian/U.S. 10-year bond yield spread ended above the day's lows as the local market retraced slightly ahead of the U.S. PPI later today. It had contracted to around the 115 basis point low seen last week, its lowest level in over two years. U.S. PPI for August seen up 0.1 percent.
